reviews.one_line_contribution: That the number of retrieved memory items injected into a ReAct agent is simultaneously a variance lever, so that the fraction of a prompt optimizer's reported validation gain attributable to pure selection bias (measured by a null-proposal optimizer) is strictly larger at k=7 than at k=0 - plus a measurement of whether common random numbers survive interactive rollouts, split into item-sharing and seed-sharing components.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal concedes both. (1) Dodge et al. 2019 'Show Your Work' owns the max-of-N validation inflation mechanism and the 'report performance as a function of search budget' prescription; P7 is literally a fit to sigma*sqrt(2 ln N), i.e. a confirmation of their formula with a measured sigma. (2) The track's own prior work already reported a null replicate matching the best real treatment and a 5-14 point re-scoring spread, which is P6 - correctly demoted to replication. What is left as novel is thinner than it looks: given P1 (sigma rises with k) and the extreme-value account the proposal itself endorses, P2 (bias rises with k) is close to an arithmetic corollary rather than an independent finding, so E1's 76,800 search rollouts are largely spent confirming a two-line derivation. On the remedy side, Miller 2024 ('Adding Error Bars to Evals') already argues for paired/variance-reduced comparison of LLM evaluations and resampling-based power analysis, which pre-empts much of the framing of E2b even if not the interactive-agent CRN decomposition. The genuinely unclaimed object is P3 (does seed-sharing buy anything once a changed prompt changes the tool queries), and that is one experiment, not a paper.
reviews.strongest_objection: E0 and E1 cannot attribute variance inflation to memory injection, because injection also moves the mean accuracy and there is no mean-variance decoupling anywhere in the protocol. Scores are binary per item, so sigma is mechanically p(1-p)/m: the track's own prior result says k=7 hurts accuracy, so the predicted sigma(k=7)/sigma(k=0) >= 1.3 in P1 can be produced entirely by the accuracy level drifting toward 0.5, with no 'lengthened and destabilized trajectories' involved at all. The proposal reports mean episode length and tool calls as corroboration but never standardizes the variance (no overdispersion ratio against the binomial baseline at the realized p, no accuracy-matched comparison), so the headline coupling survives its own primary test under an explanation that has nothing to do with memory. The same confound then propagates to P2, since null gain scales with sigma. Second, the primary k-contrast is 4 paired optimizer seeds on run-level null gain, which is itself an extreme-value statistic accumulated over 8 generations of max-of-12; the assumed between-run SD of 1.5 points is optimistic for exactly that kind of quantity, and the proposal's own escape clause (if SD > 2.2, report as directional only) means the most likely outcome of the primary experiment is 'not detected'. Third, curse fraction = null gain / real gain is a ratio with a denominator the authors' own Risk 1 says may be near zero; its 4-seed interval will be unstable or undefined, and P2's 0.15-absolute threshold on it is not defensible.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Add a length- and accuracy-matched placebo injection arm and report variance as an overdispersion ratio relative to p(1-p)/m at the realized accuracy, so that 'volume inflates variance' is separated from 'volume moves accuracy toward 0.5' and from 'more prefill tokens'. Run E1 at k in {0,3,7} rather than {0,7}: prior track work puts the harm threshold between 3 and 7, so a dose-response with the same breakpoint would be real evidence for the coupling, whereas a two-level contrast cannot distinguish dose-response from an idiosyncratic difference between two configurations. Raise E1 to 6-8 optimizer seeds per cell (the cheapest way is fewer generations or a smaller candidate pool, both of which are logged variables in E3 anyway) and pre-register null gain difference in points as the primary endpoint, dropping the curse-fraction ratio to a descriptive secondary. Draw the E2 candidate pool independently of the validation pool used to build the tensor. Finally, demote the EB rank-preservation 'result': shrinkage toward a common mean under equal allocation and equal variances is a monotone affine map of the scores, so rank preservation is a one-line observation, and P5 pre-registers that this claimed contribution is a no-op.
reviews.missing_baseline: A placebo injection arm: k=7 items that are token-count-matched but non-informative (shuffled, topically mismatched, or neutral filler distilled to the same length), evaluated in both E0 and E1. Without it, 'memory volume' is confounded with context length and with accuracy level, and a reviewer will read P1/P2 as 'longer prompts make agents noisier', which is neither new nor about memory. Secondarily missing on the remedy side: a plain fresh-validation-split rule (resample the validation pool each generation, or hold out a rotating slice) as the cheapest anti-overfitting control practitioners actually use, and an accuracy-matched k=0 condition (e.g. a weakened seed prompt) that lands at the same p as k=7, to test whether bias tracks injection or merely tracks sigma.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin, it is empty, and by the proposal's own words this is the second consecutive round with zero retrieved titles ('the literature search failed again, and returned nothing... novelty unverified'). The honesty is genuinely creditable - no fabricated citations, an explicit pre-registered query list, and a kill clause if both the k-interaction and the CRN decomposition are already published - but honesty about an unverified claim does not make the claim verified, and after two rounds the burden has not been discharged. The named collisions (Dodge 2019 for the mechanism, the track's own null replicate for P6, ProTeGi/MIPROv2/GEPA for partial mitigations) are all conceded from background knowledge, and the authors themselves flag 2025-2026 preprints on agent evaluation noise floors and winner's-curse corrections for prompt optimizers as the highest-risk unretrieved area. I could not verify that area either within the constraints of this review, so I treat novelty as unestablished rather than absent; note that Miller 2024 on error bars for evals and the general body of work on evaluation-variance quantification already cover part of the remedy framing, which raises the prior that something in the last twelve months covers the selection-bias-in-prompt-optimizers claim as well. This alone would not sink the paper, but combined with the fact that the headline is a corollary of a mechanism the authors disclaim, it means the submission currently rests on P3 - a single negative-result experiment - as its only defensibly unclaimed contribution.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That the memory injection budget k is simultaneously a variance lever and therefore a selection-bias lever: the fraction of a reflective prompt optimizer's reported validation gain that is pure winner's-curse artefact is larger at k=7 than k=0, measured with a null-proposal optimizer paired by optimizer seed, plus a measurement of whether common random numbers (item-sharing vs seed-sharing) survive in an interactive agent. I can state it, but the first half is close to a corollary of things the proposal itself already assumes.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three threats, in decreasing order. (1) Dodge et al. 2019 'Show Your Work', which the proposal correctly disclaims for the mechanism — but the disclaimer does more damage than acknowledged: given max-of-N inflation ~ sigma*sqrt(2 ln N) (which the proposal itself adopts in P7), P2 follows arithmetically from P1 plus a fixed N. If more injected context raises sigma, larger selection bias is entailed, not discovered; E1's 76,800 rollouts are then a calibration of a known formula, not a test of a new claim. (2) On the remedy side, Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification' (TRIPLE, NeurIPS 2024) frames prompt selection under a fixed evaluation budget explicitly as noisy best-arm identification and is a much closer neighbour to E2b than ProTeGi's UCB; it is not cited and not run as a baseline. (3) For P1, prompt/context-sensitivity work (Sclar et al., FormatSpread, ICLR 2024) and the long-context degradation literature ('lost in the middle' and its 2025 successors) already establish that added context moves accuracy and its dispersion; 'injecting 7 items raises run-to-run sigma by >=1.3x' will read to many reviewers as instrumentation of an expected effect. The track's own prior null replicate is correctly identified as colliding with P6 and correctly demoted.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claim is tested at n=4, with a power assumption that contradicts the hypothesis being tested. P2's primary endpoint is a within-seed paired contrast of run-level null gain across k=0 and k=7 with exactly 4 optimizer seeds (3 df), and the stated MDE of ~2.8 points depends on a *guessed* between-run SD of 1.5 points. But run-level null gain is itself a max-of-N extreme statistic whose between-run dispersion scales with the very sigma the proposal predicts is inflated at k=7 — so under H1 the k=7 arm has the larger between-run SD by construction, the paired differences are heteroscedastic, and the design is least powered exactly where it needs precision. The proposal's own escape hatch ("if between-run SD exceeds 2.2 we report P2 as directional") concedes the likeliest outcome: the primary claim is unresolvable and the paper falls back to E2, which the risk section itself calls the part most exposed to being scooped. Compounding this, the derived endpoint 'curse fraction = null gain / real gain' with a threshold of 0.15 absolute has a denominator that this track's own prior work suggests may be near zero on a 7B agent (optimizer gain was redistribution, not accuracy); a ratio with a near-zero, noisy denominator across 4 seeds is not an estimable quantity, and no rule is given for what happens when real gain is <=0 in some seeds.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Re-budget E1 rather than add compute: cut generations from 8 to 5 and candidates from 12 to 8 (1,600 rollouts/run) and spend the savings on 8-10 optimizer seeds per cell, so the primary paired contrast has usable df and the between-run SD is estimated rather than assumed; N is a controlled variable in P7 anyway, so a smaller N costs a design point, not a claim. Make null gain in accuracy points the sole primary endpoint and demote curse fraction to a descriptive ratio reported only when real gain exceeds the null-replicate floor. Add the accuracy-matched control described under missing_baseline so the k-contrast is not confounded with headroom. State the decoding temperature and include a greedy-vs-sampled arm in E0 — if evaluation is near-greedy, the decoding variance component and the whole seed-sharing half of P3 are degenerate by construction. Build the E2 tensor from candidates harvested at both k=0 and k=7 (10 each) so selection-rule conclusions can be stated as a function of the injection budget rather than only inside the noisy arm. Finally, drop P5 from the novelty list: that a common shrinkage factor applied to deviations from a common mean preserves ranks under equal allocation is an algebraic identity, not a finding; keep it as a one-paragraph remark and let the empirical part be the unequal-allocation case.
reviews.missing_baseline: An accuracy- and length-matched k=0 control. At k=7 the seed prompt is known (from this track's own prior result) to score *worse* than at k=0, so a larger null-optimizer gain at k=7 is fully explained by more headroom, regression toward the mean on a bounded binary metric, and lower baseline accuracy sitting nearer the steep part of the binomial variance curve p(1-p) — none of which require 'memory inflates selection bias'. The plan has no arm that holds baseline accuracy fixed while varying k, so P2's contrast cannot distinguish its own mechanism from a floor effect. Two cheap controls fix this: (i) a k=0 arm with a deliberately weakened seed prompt matched to the k=7 baseline accuracy; (ii) a k=7-token-matched arm injecting irrelevant or shuffled bank items, which holds context length and episode length fixed while removing retrieved-experience content, separating 'volume as tokens' from 'volume as memory'. Secondary omissions: no best-arm-identification/TRIPLE-style baseline in E2b, and no k=0 outcome tensor in E2.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is the weakest section and, by the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, it materially lowers my scores. The check reports *zero* successful searches — every query errored — and self-labels 'novelty unverified, for the second consecutive round.' The honesty is real and I credit the refusal to fabricate citations, but a submission arriving twice with no retrieved literature has not established novelty, and the section's own text identifies the highest-risk niche (2025-2026 preprints on agent evaluation noise floors, benchmark reproducibility audits, and winner's-curse corrections for prompt optimizers) as active and plausible for a collision. I cannot name a specific 2026 preprint from here, but the named risks are concrete: best-arm-identification/fixed-budget selection for prompt optimization is an existing published line (TRIPLE, NeurIPS 2024) that the section does not mention at all, and inference-nondeterminism / eval-noise-floor reporting for LLM agents is a heavily populated 2025-2026 area. Separately, the pre-registered kill-switch is set so narrowly as to be near-vacuous: the project is killed only if a single paper reports *both* the k-interaction *and* the CRN item/seed decomposition for interactive agents. Almost no preprint will satisfy that conjunction, so the clause functions as insurance rather than as a commitment; a per-claim demotion rule (as already written for the P1/P2 case) should be the operative standard, and the search log must land before compute is spent, not alongside it.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That the memory-injection budget k is not only an accuracy lever but a *variance* lever, so a prompt optimizer searching over a k=7 agent captures a strictly larger fraction of its reported validation gain as pure selection bias than at k=0 — measured with a null (identity/paraphrase-proposal) optimizer paired by optimizer seed — plus a measured decomposition of whether common random numbers survive interactive rollouts at all.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three bodies threaten different pieces, and the proposal has already conceded two of them. (1) Dodge et al., 'Show Your Work' (2019) and its follow-up 'Expected Validation Performance and Estimation of a Random Variable's Maximum' (NAACL 2021) own the max-of-N inflation mechanism and the budget-indexed reporting rule; the proposal disclaims this outright, which is honest but removes the mechanism from the contribution. (2) The track's own prior null replicate and 5-14 point re-scoring spread own the phenomenon; P6 is self-labelled replication. (3) The threat to what *remains* is the long-context/distraction literature — Liu et al., 'Lost in the Middle' (2023), Shi et al., 'Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context' (2023), Levy et al., 'Same Task, More Tokens' (2024) — which already establishes that more injected context degrades and destabilizes generation. P1 ('k=7 lengthens trajectories and inflates sigma') is close to a restatement of that in agent clothing, and the proposal offers no arm that separates 'memory items' from 'more tokens.' A fourth threat is to the *instrument*: Sclar et al. (ICLR 2024) and Mizrahi et al. (TACL 2024) show semantics-preserving prompt variation produces large, real accuracy swings, which undercuts the assumption that a judge-verified-paraphrase null arm measures only selection bias.
reviews.strongest_objection: Both primary novelty claims are underpowered by construction, and the proposal says so itself. P1 estimates a variance ratio from 8 replicates per cell: with ~7 df on each side, the 95% CI for a variance ratio spans roughly a factor of 5, so sigma(k=7)/sigma(k=0) must be observed at ~2.2x before the CI on the ratio excludes 1 — yet P1 predicts 1.3x. Measurement note 7 concedes 'a true ratio near 1.3 may go undetected,' meaning a *primary* prediction is designed so that its own predicted effect size is undetectable, at a cost of 9,600 rollouts. P2 is worse: it is a 4-pair paired test, and the claimed MDE of ~2.8 points appears to have been imported from the n=1,200 item-level McNemar calculation in note 1. A one-sample t-test with n=4 needs d~2.2, so at the stated between-run SD of 1.5 the true MDE is ~3.4 points and higher still if the paired-difference SD (not the between-run SD) is 1.5*sqrt(2); the pre-registered threshold of 3 points sits below it. Compounding this, the headline is confounded: score variance for a binary metric is p(1-p)/m, so if k=7 moves accuracy toward 0.5 (the track's prior work says injection at 7 items *harms* accuracy), sigma rises mechanically and the 'coupling' is a base-rate artifact, not evidence that memory volume amplifies the curse. Reporting bias in accuracy points rather than in sigma units makes this indistinguishable. The result is a plan whose well-powered components (E2's cached tensor, E3's design rule) are self-labelled replication, baseline transport, or derived from the underpowered E0/E1 inputs, while the parts carrying the novelty claim will most likely return 'not detected.'
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Reallocate the envelope toward the claim that carries the novelty. (1) Add a content-matched placebo at k=7 (shuffled/off-query retrieved items, or token-matched filler) so P1 can attribute variance inflation to retrieved experience rather than to context length — without it P1 is a known long-context result. (2) Fix P1's estimator: 8 replicates cannot resolve 1.3x. Either raise replicates to ~30 per cell (these are cheap eval rollouts; the 48,000-rollout E2 tensor is oversized relative to K=20 candidates) or estimate sigma from the m-subsampling curve with a paired bootstrap across k on shared items. (3) Make P2 an actual interaction: run E1 at k in {0,3,7}, since the track's own causal lever is the 3-vs-7 contrast, and buy optimizer seeds by cutting generations (8x12x50 = 4,800 rollouts per run; halving generations roughly doubles seeds). (4) Report null gain standardized by the condition's own sigma, and drop 'curse fraction' as the primary derived quantity — it is a ratio whose denominator (real gain) the proposal's own Risk 1 admits may be near zero, so its 4-seed interval is meaningless. (5) State and test the transport assumption that null-arm bias estimates real-arm bias: the exact-copy null has perfectly correlated candidates, the real arm does not, and the correlation discount in P7 is exactly what differs between them — move ablation (f) into E1 rather than E2. (6) Demote the EB rank-preservation 'separation' to a remark, or state it correctly: shrinkage toward a common mean is rank-preserving only under homoskedastic candidate variances, and binomial variance p(1-p)/m is not homoskedastic even at equal m, so the 'analytic' claim is either trivial or false as written. (7) Run the literature search before spending compute, as pre-registered.
reviews.missing_baseline: A content-matched / length-matched placebo injection arm at k=7: seven retrieved items that are topically plausible but query-irrelevant (or shuffled across items, or token-matched filler), evaluated in both E0 and E1. Without it, every P1/P2 effect is equally explained by 'longer, more distractable contexts' and the paper's claim to belong to the memory track collapses. Secondarily, E1 omits k=3 entirely, so the design cannot show that selection bias tracks the same dose-response curve (harm at 7, none at 3) that motivated the whole proposal — a two-point contrast cannot distinguish a monotone volume effect from an arbitrary threshold. A third gap: E2b compares ten selection rules on a pool of only K=20 candidates, all harvested from the four real k=7 runs; the bootstrap over the candidate pool, not over the 1,200 items, is the binding interval, and 20 survivorship-selected candidates cannot resolve the 1-2 point differences P4 predicts.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is a self-declared failure: zero searches completed, zero titles retrieved, for the second consecutive round, with the authors correctly refusing to call that novelty. Per the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this alone caps novelty. I credit the honesty and the pre-registered kill clause ('if a paper reports both the k-interaction and the CRN item/seed decomposition, the project is killed'), but a proposal cannot outsource its own novelty verification to a post-acceptance appendix. I cannot verify 2026 preprints, so I state only what I can: the exact niche the authors themselves flag as highest-risk — evaluation-noise floors for LLM agents, winner's-curse and multiple-comparison corrections for prompt optimizers, and statistical protocols for LLM evals — is demonstrably active and already has anchored entries (Miller, 'Adding Error Bars to Evals,' arXiv 2411.00640; Madaan et al., 'Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks,' 2024; Card et al., 'With Little Power Comes Great Responsibility,' EMNLP 2020; Dodge et al., NAACL 2021), none of which appear in the Related Work despite bearing directly on the MDE, power, and shrinkage arguments the proposal builds its protocol on. Their absence suggests the background-knowledge pass was as incomplete as the search. The burden is on the authors to show the k x selection-bias interaction and the item/seed CRN decomposition are unclaimed; as submitted, that burden is unmet.
